newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo PGM futures end sharply higher on NY gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo PGM futures end sharply higher on NY gains.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum and palladium futures ended sharply higher on Friday, due to price gains in the New York market overnight, traders said.
The benchmark June 1998 palladium rose by its 22 yen daily limit to 565 yen per gram by the close. The June 1998 platinum contract ended up 26 yen at 1,389 yen.
"The New York market's gains encouraged local investors to cover their short positions," a brokerage house trader said.
Russia's first platinum shipment following a six-month suspension finally arrived at Tokyo's Narita airport on Thursday, a senior official of a large bullion house said.

"The first shipment of Russian platinum arrived in Tokyo yesterday, and if they can keep delivering platinum for at least the next three months, supply concerns in the Japanese market will be erased," the official said.
He did not specify the size of the shipment. He said a second platinum shipment, for a foreign bullion house, would probably arrive in Tokyo at the weekend.
World platinum and palladium prices have soared since the beginning of this year due to the suspension of supplies by the Russian platinum group metal export agency, Almazjuvelirexport.
Gold futures ended higher across the board. Prices were 10 to 14 yen higher, with the June 1998 contract up 12 yen at 1,197 yen per gram.
Bullion was quoted $323.45/85 per ounce at 0755 GMT, compared with $324.00/50 in New York overnight and a 12-year low fix of $315.75 in London earlier this month.
Silver futures were mixed. The June 1998 was down 0.3 yen at 162.3 yen per 10 grams.
